title: Strengthening diagnostic capacity for viral hemorrhagic fevers in Forest Guinea: advances in Lassa fever case detection
abstract: Abstract Viral hemorrhagic fevers (VHFs) remain a major public health threat in resource-limited settings. The 2014–2016 Ebola epidemic exposed critical gaps in laboratory preparedness and diagnostic capacity in most-at-risk countries, including Guinea. In order to implement sustainable in-country laboratory capacity for early detection and rapid response to VHF outbreaks, a decentralized diagnostics laboratory strengthening program started in the forested region of Guinea in Guéckédou (2017) and N’Zérékoré (2021). Between 2017 and 2024, a total of 4683 samples from suspected VHF cases were tested across the two laboratories. Of those, 47 (1%) were identified as positive for VHFs by molecular testing, including the 2021 Ebola virus disease resurgence and Marburg virus disease emergence samples, for which the laboratories supported rapid outbreak detection and response. Notably, 30 Lassa fever cases were laboratory-confirmed with a case fatality rate of 67.9%. Of those, 50.0% and 27.6% of the cases originating from the Guéckédou and N’Zérékoré prefecture, respectively. Prior to this program, Lassa fever detection in Guinea remained anecdotic. One case of yellow fever and one of dengue were also identified by molecular assays. The establishment of locally embedded laboratory capacity enhanced VHFs preparedness, surveillance, and response in Guinea, supporting Lassa fever epidemiology and health-system resilience.

full_text: Given the current state of medical research and the ongoing threat posed by vector-borne illnesses, a multisectoral collaboration using one health approach is needed to bolster our resistance to these dangerous adversaries. Dengue Fever, a vector- borne disease, continues to cast its shadow across communities worldwide, posing a significant threat to public health. Dengue also known as bone-break fever is a viral illness that spread from mosquitoes (Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus) to human beings. This virus has four different serotypes namely DENV-1,2,3,4. While DENV frequently results in an acute flu-like illness, a significant portion of infections lead to mild illness with over 80% of cases exhibiting no symptoms Sequential . infection increases the risk of severe dengue. Immunization to one serotype does not offer cross immunity to other serotypes. Recent years have witnessed a staggering surge in Dengue cases with an estimate of 96 million symptomatic cases and about 40,000 deaths 1 annually in over 129 countries, according to WHO. Pakistan is home to the endemic Dengue fever, which is transmitted throughout the year with seasonal peaks. Initially dengue fever was documented to have occurred in 1994, however a sharp increase in incidence and the yearly epidemic 2 trend started in November 2005 in Karachi. The worst flooding in the history of Pakistan has further increased the number of reported dengue cases in 2022 between January and September as compared to previous four years. As per the National Institute of Health, the country has documented a cumulative of 25,932 confirmed cases with reported 62 deaths. About 74% of the cases were recorded in the month of September alone. As of September 22, province wise distribution was available for 83% (21777 cases) of the total, revealing that 32% (6888 cases) were documented in Sindh and 29%(6255 cases) in 3 Punjab( including Islamabad Capital Territory), followed by Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan. A recent data collected by European Centre for Disease Prevention and Control indicated that case notification per 100,000 population in Pakistan remained below100 during December 2022 to 4 November 2023. Since there is no particular cure for dengue, prompt case identification, spotting any early warning signs of a severe infection, and efficient management of cases are essential components of patient care that can reduce the mortality rate of severe infections to less than 1%. To mitigate the control of dengue vector, Pakistan's Emergency Plan of Action (EPoA), Dengue Response is presently being implemented. By distributing long-lasting insecticidal nets (LLINs), mosquito repellent, spraying, and fumigating mosquito breeding places; this initiative seeks to minimize the spread of transmission of vector and establish preventative measures among susceptible populations by 5 increasing community awareness. Furthermore, Ministry of Health in collaboration of global funds has initiated a Vector Management Program to dengue virus. This comprehensive approach involves weekly technical committee meetings led by Ministry of Health and establishment of dengue 1 2 3 Warda Samad, Mehwish Akhtar, Shahid Mehmood Sethi FROM CRISIS TO CONTROL: NAVIGATING THE DENGUE CHALLENGE EDITORIAL JAIMC 227 JAIMC Vol. 21 No. 4 October - December 2023 1-3. From Crisis to Control: Navigating the Dengue Challenge. JAIMC 2023; 21(04): 227-228 FROM CRISIS TO CONTROL: NAVIGATING THE DENGUE CHALLENGE 228 JAIMC Vol. 21 No. 4 October - December 2023 6 counters in all health facilities. Pakistan has enormous challenges in its fight against mosquito-borne illness, chiefly brought on by its 7 climate, urbanization, and low public knowledge. In order to successfully address these issues and lessen the effects of dengue and malaria epidemics, implementation of comprehensive solutions that include targeted public health education initiatives, climate-responsive vector control, and urban design considerations must be taken. A ray of optimism is provided by recent breakthroughs despite the obstacles in control of dengue. Faster and more precise diagnosis of Dengue infections is made possible by modern diagnostic technology including advanced imaging and quick testing. The development and introduction of Dengue vaccines, together with the historic approval of several formulations, represents a major advancement in prophylactic care. A live recombinant tetra valent dengue vaccine (CYD- TDV) has been developed to be used in seropositive individuals after pre-vaccination screening of the individual for serum IgG antibodies against dengue. This vaccine is licensed for use in 20 countries and given as three dose series of 0,6 and 12 months to individuals aged 9-45 years residing in the dengue endemic areas. Moreover, 5 more vaccine are under trial with 2 vaccines in phase 3 of clinical trial and showing promising results. In this scenario, it is hard to deny that preventive strategies will see a radical transition in the coming time by introduction of vaccine against dengue. It is the need of the moment to realize the importance of one health approach and take appropriate steps in accordance with the principles of primary health care using inter-sectoral collaboration of all the government as well as private organizations working in synchronization along with active community participation to achieve a common cause- the control of Dengue. title: Use of time-series forecasting of dengue incidence based on meteorological predictors in Western Nepal
abstract: Dengue is an emerging public health concern in Nepal, with rapidly increasing incidence and recurrent outbreaks, particularly in Gandaki Province. Climatic factors play a crucial role in dengue transmission dynamics, yet high-resolution time-series analyses integrating both statistical and machine-learning approaches remain limited in this setting. We conducted a time-series study using weekly dengue incidence data from January 2020 to December 2025 in Gandaki Province, Nepal. Meteorological variables (temperature, precipitation, humidity, and wind speed) were obtained from the ERA5-Land dataset. Seasonal-trend decomposition, correlation, cross-correlation, and negative binomial regression analyses were performed to assess climatic associations with lag effects. Forecasting models including Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), SARIMA with exogenous variables (SARIMAX), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were developed and compared using rolling-origin cross-validation based on MAE and RMSE. A total of 34,364 dengue cases were reported during the study period, with pronounced post-monsoon peaks in September–October. Seasonal decomposition showed that annual seasonality accounted for a substantial proportion of the temporal variability in dengue incidence. Temperature was the strongest and most consistent climatic predictor, remaining significantly associated with dengue incidence in negative binomial regression across contemporaneous and 1–2 month lag models (IRR: 1.145–1.187, all p < 0.05). Structural break analysis identified a significant shift in transmission dynamics around 2024–2025. Among the forecasting models, SARIMAX demonstrated superior out-of-sample predictive performance (MAE: 240.35; RMSE: 397.51) compared with SARIMA, while XGBoost achieved comparable average accuracy but showed greater variability and reduced stability during periods of structural change. Forecasts indicate continued seasonal outbreaks with moderate epidemic activity through 2027. Dengue transmission in Gandaki Province is strongly seasonal and climate-sensitive, with temperature emerging as the most robust climatic predictor after accounting for overdispersion. SARIMAX models incorporating meteorological variables provided the best out-of-sample forecasting performance and offer an interpretable framework for climate-informed dengue early warning systems. Integrating such forecasting approaches into routine surveillance may enhance preparedness and support timely public health interventions in Nepal.

Meteorological variables (temperature, precipitation, humidity, and wind speed) were obtained from the ERA5-Land dataset. Seasonal-trend decomposition, correlation, cross-correlation, and negative binomial regression analyses were performed to assess climatic associations with lag effects. Forecasting models including Seasonal Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (SARIMA), SARIMA with exogenous variables (SARIMAX), and Extreme Gradient Boosting (XGBoost) were developed and compared using rolling-origin cross-validation based on MAE and RMSE. A total of 34,364 dengue cases were reported during the study period, with pronounced post-monsoon peaks in September–October. Seasonal decomposition showed that annual seasonality accounted for a substantial proportion of the temporal variability in dengue incidence. Temperature was the strongest and most consistent climatic predictor, remaining significantly associated with dengue incidence in negative binomial regression across contemporaneous and 1–2 month lag models (IRR: 1.145–1.187, all p < 0.05). Structural break analysis identified a significant shift in transmission dynamics around 2024–2025. Among the forecasting models, SARIMAX demonstrated superior out-of-sample predictive performance (MAE: 240.35; RMSE: 397.51) compared with SARIMA, while XGBoost achieved comparable average accuracy but showed greater variability and reduced stability during periods of structural change. Forecasts indicate continued seasonal outbreaks with moderate epidemic activity through 2027. Dengue transmission in Gandaki Province is strongly seasonal and climate-sensitive, with temperature emerging as the most robust climatic predictor after accounting for overdispersion. SARIMAX models incorporating meteorological variables provided the best out-of-sample forecasting performance and offer an interpretable framework for climate-informed dengue early warning systems. Integrating such forecasting approaches into routine surveillance may enhance preparedness and support timely public health interventions in Nepal.

abstract_zh: 登革热已成为尼泊尔日益突出的公共卫生问题,其发病率迅速上升,且在甘达基省反复暴发。气候因素在登革热发病率动态中起着关键作用,但在该地区结合统计学和机器学习方法的高分辨率时间序列分析仍较为有限。我们使用尼泊尔甘达基省2020年1月至2025年12月的每周登革热发病率数据,开展了一项时间序列研究。气象变量(温度、降水量、湿度和风速)来自ERA5-Land数据集。通过季节性趋势分解、相关性、交叉相关性以及负二项回归分析,评估了气候因素与滞后效应之间的关联。我们开发并比较了包括季节性自回归积分滑动平均(SARIMA)、带外生变量的SARIMA(SARIMAX)以及极端梯度提升(XGBoost)在内的预测模型,采用基于MAE和RMSE的滚动起源交叉验证方法。研究期间共报告了34,364例登革热病例,其中9月至10月出现显著的季风后高峰。季节性分解显示,年度季节性因素在登革热发病率的时间变化中占了相当大的比例。温度是最强且最一致的气候预测因子,在负二项回归分析中,温度在同期及1至2个月滞后期模型中均与登革热发病率显著相关(IRR:1.145–1.187,所有p < 0.05)。结构突变分析发现,2024–2025年间登革热动态发生了显著变化。在预测模型中,SARIMAX在样本外预测表现优于SARIMA(MAE:240.35;RMSE:397.51),而XGBoost在平均准确性上表现相当,但在结构突变期间表现出更大的波动性和更低的稳定性。预测表明,到2027年登革热仍将呈现季节性暴发,且流行活动中等。甘达基省的登革热发病率具有明显的季节性和气候敏感性,温度在考虑过度分散后成为最稳健的气候预测因子。纳入气象变量的SARIMAX模型提供了最佳的样本外预测性能,并为基于气候的登革热早期预警系统提供了可解释的框架。将此类预测方法整合到常规监测中,可能有助于提高尼泊尔的应对能力,并支持及时的公共卫生干预措施。

Revised: July 16, 2026. 668 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.34 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ An Adaptive Gated Fusion-based Multimodal Framework for Influential Actor Identification in Dengue Haemorrhagic Fever Information Dissemination on YouTube Ayu Eka Lestari1 Wiwik Anggraeni1* 1Department of Information Systems, Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Surabaya, Indonesia * Corresponding author’s Email: wiwik@is.its.ac.id Abstract: Dengue hemorrhagic fever remains a critical public health concern in Indonesia, and YouTube has become a major channel for health information. Identifying influential actors is essential for public health communication, yet existing social network analysis relies on text and ignores visual signals such as video thumbnails. This study proposes a multimodal framework based on Adaptive Gated Fusion that combines text and visual features without any audio modality. Textual features from IndoBERT and visual features from ResNet-50 are fused adaptively per dimension, aggregated per channel, and used to build a content-based co-audience network analysed with PageRank. Using 33,233 Indonesian comments from 5,365 videos across 1,129 collected channels (1,084 retained after language filtering) over 2021 to 2025, an ablation study with stratified five-fold cross-validation shows the fused representation reaches 79.52 percent accuracy and 78.42 percent macro F1, outperforming text and visual baselines. KOMPASTV, Kata Dokter, and Halodoc emerged as the most influential actors. Keywords: Adaptive gated fusion, Co-audience graph, Dengue haemorrhagic fever, IndoBERT, PageRank, ResNet- 50, Sentiment analysis, Social network analysis, YouTube. 1. Introduction Dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF) is a tropical infectious disease transmitted through the bites of the Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, and it is one of the major public health burdens in Indonesia. The World Health Organization (WHO) recorded 149,866 confirmed DHF cases in Indonesia up to 1 July 2024, an increase of roughly threefold compared with the same period in 2023, spread across 465 regencies/cities in 38 provinces [1]. Although the case trend declined in 2025, DHF remains a health priority that requires effective prevention strategies and public education [2]. As case numbers rise, the Indonesian public increasingly relies on social media as a source of health information. YouTube has a unique characteristic as a multimodal platform: its content combines visual elements in the form of video thumbnails and textual elements in the form of user comments, which jointly shape public health perceptions and behaviour [3]. However, the openness of this platform also presents challenges, because the information that circulates is not always accurate and can negatively affect public health decisions [4]. Identifying the most influential actors in the dissemination of DHF information is crucial for designing well-targeted interventions. Social Network Analysis (SNA) has proven effective for this purpose: centrality metrics such as PageRank, degree centrality, and betweenness centrality are widely used to measure the level of influence of a node in a network [5], while community detection through the Louvain algorithm enables actors to be grouped according to similar interaction patterns [6]. However, previous research applying SNA to health information has been dominated by text-based platforms such as Twitter and Facebook [7]. As a result, when influence is measured solely from textual signals, the visual dimension that also Received: June 18, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 669 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.34 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ determines the reach of content, particularly thumbnails on platforms such as YouTube, is entirely overlooked. On multimodal platforms, measuring influence from text alone risks misjudging which actors shape public discourse, so a representation capable of capturing both modalities simultaneously is needed. In natural language processing, pre-trained transformer-based models such as BERT have transformed the way text is represented, and IndoBERT in particular is able to understand the context of the Indonesian language better than multilingual models [8]; this capability has been exploited for sentiment analysis of YouTube comments [9] and emotion classification [10]. In computer vision, ResNet-50 is a deep learning architecture widely used for visual feature extraction because its residual learning approach enables the construction of deep networks with effective training [11]. Multimodal approaches that fuse textual and visual features have been shown to improve analytical accuracy compared with unimodal approaches [12]. In particular, the Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF) technique combines the two modalities through a gating mechanism that assigns dynamic per-dimension weights between text and visual features [13], so that the contribution of each modality is not set uniformly but is adjusted to the characteristics of each piece of content. AGF therefore has the potential to address the limitations of text-based analysis by integrating the visual signals that have so far been ignored in identifying influential actors on multimodal platforms. Based on the review above, two main gaps can be identified. First, studies on influential actors in health information still focus on text-based platforms, whereas YouTube, which combines text and visuals, has not been widely studied. Second, SNA research generally still uses only a single type of data, so the visual information in video content has not been optimally exploited; in particular, the combination of IndoBERT and ResNet-50 through adaptive fusion to build a co-audience network has never been explored. To address these gaps, this study proposes an AGF- based multimodal framework for identifying influential actors in the dissemination of DHF information on YouTube. The main objectives of this study are described as follows: 1. Multimodal Representation: integrating IndoBERT textual embeddings and ResNet-50 visual embeddings through Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), which assigns adaptive per- dimension weights across modalities, without relying on the audio modality. 2. Network Construction: building a co-audience graph based on multimodal content similarity derived from AGF, rather than explicit interactions, and applying PageRank-based SNA to identify influential channels together with their community structure. 3. Sentiment Profiling: fine-tuning a RoBERTa model for Indonesian text to build sentiment profiles for each influential channel. 4. Empirical Validation: conducting an ablation study with stratified 5-fold cross-validation on seven modality configurations to evaluate whether the adaptively fused multimodal representation outperforms the unimodal text and visual baselines in sentiment classification accuracy. The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 reviews related works on multimodal sentiment analysis, social network analysis, and sentiment analysis of health content. Section 3 describes the dataset and the proposed AGF-based multimodal framework. Section 4 presents the experimental results and discussion. Finally, Section 5 concludes the paper and outlines directions for future work. 2. Related works 2.1 Multimodal sentiment analysis Multimodal sentiment analysis combines information from several modalities, typically text, audio, and visual, to produce a richer representation than a single modality alone. Gandhi et al. [14] concluded that multimodal fusion methods outperform unimodal approaches across various datasets, and Zhu et al. [15] reinforced this finding through a survey of fusion methods that emphasised that selecting the appropriate fusion strategy is highly decisive for model performance. In a domain similar to this study, Kothuri and RajaLakshmi [16] proposed the MALO-LSTM model, which combines text, audio, and visual modalities for sentiment analysis on YouTube; the model achieved 98.62% accuracy and showed that combining the three modalities yields better results than using the modalities separately. Recent research emphasises the importance of adaptive fusion mechanisms, that is, mechanisms that adjust the weight of each modality according to context. Wang et al. [17] proposed a multimodal transformer that assigns modality weights adaptively, whereas Lu et al. [18] developed a gated-fusion- based framework that has been shown to filter signals across modalities through a sigmoid gate that dynamically determines the magnitude of each Received: June 18, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 670 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.34 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ modality's contribution [19]. However, most of these methods were developed for English-language data and still rely on the audio modality, so the potential of the visual modality in the form of thumbnails, the primary signal on platforms such as YouTube, has not been optimally exploited, particularly for Indonesian-language content. 2.2 Social network analysis for influential actor identification Social Network Analysis (SNA) is widely used to identify key actors in online information networks. The PageRank algorithm, originally designed to rank web pages [20] was later adapted to the social network context, measuring the influence of a node not only from the number of connections but also from their quality. Rashidi et al. [21] developed a method to predict influential nodes based on local communities and user reaction information, and the results showed that nodes with high PageRank values tend to be effective information spreaders. Similarly, data-driven frameworks combine several centrality metrics such as degree centrality, betweenness centrality, and PageRank to make node rankings more accurate [22]. In the health context, identifying influential actors is highly important for designing public communication strategies. A qualitative study by Green et al. showed that digital opinion leaders play an important role in disseminating dengue prevention information, including in Indonesia [23]. However, most studies still build relationships between users from explicit interactions such as retweets and mentions, even though users who discuss similar topics do not necessarily interact with one another. Therefore, approaches based on multimodal embeddings that can capture content similarity remain underexplored. 2.3 Sentiment analysis of health content on social media Sentiment analysis of health content on social media can provide insight into how the public perceives a disease. In the case of dengue, Laguitan et al. [24] found that the quality and reliability of information circulating on YouTube vary widely, so not all sources have the same credibility and it is important to identify trustworthy sources. In Indonesia, Putri et al. [25] used IndoBERT to analyse public sentiment toward various public issues, whereas Mahakerty et al. [26] integrated Indonesian- language Twitter sentiment analysis into a deep- learning-based disease prediction model. These findings show that sentiment analysis can serve as a useful supplementary source of information for understanding the dynamics of disease spread in society. 2.4 Research gap Based on the literature review above, there are three research gaps centred on the suboptimal use of multimodal representations. First, research on multimodal sentiment analysis is still dominated by English-language data and rarely focuses on the Indonesian language, particularly in the health domain. Second, most multimodal methods rely on the audio modality, whereas the combination of text and visual thumbnails, which is precisely the primary signal on platforms such as YouTube, has not been widely studied. Third, the construction of co- audience networks to identify influential actors still depends on explicit interactions and has not exploited cross-modal content similarity, so the visual dimension that also determines content reach is overlooked. These gaps underscore the need for an Indonesian-language multimodal framework that explicitly combines the text and visual modalities to identify influential actors in the dissemination of dengue information on YouTube. Unlike previous research, the main novelty of this study lies in integrating IndoBERT text representations and ResNet-50 thumbnail visual features through Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), which assigns adaptive per-dimension weights across modalities without relying on the audio modality. The resulting multimodal fused representation is then used to build a co-audience network based on content similarity rather than explicit interactions, and the contribution of each modality is verified through an ablation study so that the advantage of the multimodal approach can be demonstrated empirically against the unimodal text and visual baselines. 3. Material and method This section describes the dataset and the research procedure used to identify influential actors in the dissemination of dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF) information on YouTube through a multimodal approach. The overall research workflow is presented in Fig. 1. 3.1 Dataset This study uses comment data and video thumbnails related to dengue haemorrhagic fever Received: June 18, 2026. The collected raw data came from 5,365 unique videos across 1,129 YouTube channels. Each data entry includes the comment text, video metadata (title, view count, and publication date), and the video thumbnail image. 3.2 Method This study applies a multimodal framework consisting of nine main stages: data collection, preprocessing, feature extraction, multimodal fusion through Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), channel-level aggregation, co-audience graph construction, social network analysis, sentiment analysis, and evaluation through an ablation study. The complete research process is shown in Fig. 1. 3.2.1. Preprocessing The preprocessing stage was carried out to produce clean and standardised data. This process comprises four steps. First, noise removal of URLs, mentions (@), hashtags (#), numbers, and special characters. Second, duplicate removal to avoid redundancy. Third, language filtering using the langdetect library to retain only Indonesian language comments. Fourth, removal of comments shorter than five words. After preprocessing, 33,233 valid comments were obtained, or 91.5% of the original corpus, which were then aligned with the related video thumbnails. 3.2.2. Multimodal feature extraction Feature extraction was carried out in parallel for the two modalities. For the text modality, each comment was encoded using IndoBERT (indobert- base-pl) [8] a BERT-based language model trained on a large Indonesian-language corpus. The token representation from the final encoder layer was used as the sentence embedding, producing a 768- dimensional vector for each comment. For the visual modality, each video thumbnail was processed using the ResNet-50 architecture [11] pre-trained on the ImageNet dataset. The final classification layer was removed, so the output taken was a 2,048-dimensional feature vector from the global average pooling layer. Each thumbnail was resized to 224 × 224 pixels before inference. The residual learning approach in ResNet-50 enables the construction of deep networks with effective training [11]. 3.2.3. Keywords: Adaptive gated fusion, Co-audience graph, Dengue haemorrhagic fever, IndoBERT, PageRank, ResNet- 50, Sentiment analysis, Social network analysis, YouTube. 1. Introduction Dengue haemorrhagic fever (DHF) is a tropical infectious disease transmitted through the bites of the Aedes aegypti and Aedes albopictus mosquitoes, and it is one of the major public health burdens in Indonesia. The World Health Organization (WHO) recorded 149,866 confirmed DHF cases in Indonesia up to 1 July 2024, an increase of roughly threefold compared with the same period in 2023, spread across 465 regencies/cities in 38 provinces [1]. Although the case trend declined in 2025, DHF remains a health priority that requires effective prevention strategies and public education [2]. As case numbers rise, the Indonesian public increasingly relies on social media as a source of health information. YouTube has a unique characteristic as a multimodal platform: its content combines visual elements in the form of video thumbnails and textual elements in the form of user comments, which jointly shape public health perceptions and behaviour [3]. However, the openness of this platform also presents challenges, because the information that circulates is not always accurate and can negatively affect public health decisions [4]. Identifying the most influential actors in the dissemination of DHF information is crucial for designing well-targeted interventions. Social Network Analysis (SNA) has proven effective for this purpose: centrality metrics such as PageRank, degree centrality, and betweenness centrality are widely used to measure the level of influence of a node in a network [5], while community detection through the Louvain algorithm enables actors to be grouped according to similar interaction patterns [6]. However, previous research applying SNA to health information has been dominated by text-based platforms such as Twitter and Facebook [7]. As a result, when influence is measured solely from textual signals, the visual dimension that also Received: June 18, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 669 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.34 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ determines the reach of content, particularly thumbnails on platforms such as YouTube, is entirely overlooked. On multimodal platforms, measuring influence from text alone risks misjudging which actors shape public discourse, so a representation capable of capturing both modalities simultaneously is needed. In natural language processing, pre-trained transformer-based models such as BERT have transformed the way text is represented, and IndoBERT in particular is able to understand the context of the Indonesian language better than multilingual models [8]; this capability has been exploited for sentiment analysis of YouTube comments [9] and emotion classification [10]. In computer vision, ResNet-50 is a deep learning architecture widely used for visual feature extraction because its residual learning approach enables the construction of deep networks with effective training [11]. Multimodal approaches that fuse textual and visual features have been shown to improve analytical accuracy compared with unimodal approaches [12]. In particular, the Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF) technique combines the two modalities through a gating mechanism that assigns dynamic per-dimension weights between text and visual features [13], so that the contribution of each modality is not set uniformly but is adjusted to the characteristics of each piece of content. AGF therefore has the potential to address the limitations of text-based analysis by integrating the visual signals that have so far been ignored in identifying influential actors on multimodal platforms. Based on the review above, two main gaps can be identified. First, studies on influential actors in health information still focus on text-based platforms, whereas YouTube, which combines text and visuals, has not been widely studied. Second, SNA research generally still uses only a single type of data, so the visual information in video content has not been optimally exploited; in particular, the combination of IndoBERT and ResNet-50 through adaptive fusion to build a co-audience network has never been explored. To address these gaps, this study proposes an AGF- based multimodal framework for identifying influential actors in the dissemination of DHF information on YouTube. The main objectives of this study are described as follows: 1. Multimodal Representation: integrating IndoBERT textual embeddings and ResNet-50 visual embeddings through Adaptive Gated Fusion (AGF), which assigns adaptive per- dimension weights across modalities, without relying on the audio modality. 2. Network Construction: building a co-audience graph based on multimodal content similarity derived from AGF, rather than explicit interactions, and applying PageRank-based SNA to identify influential channels together with their community structure. 3. Sentiment Profiling: fine-tuning a RoBERTa model for Indonesian text to build sentiment profiles for each influential channel. 4. Empirical Validation: conducting an ablation study with stratified 5-fold cross-validation on seven modality configurations to evaluate whether the adaptively fused multimodal representation outperforms the unimodal text and visual baselines in sentiment classification accuracy. The remainder of this paper is organized as follows. Section 2 reviews related works on multimodal sentiment analysis, social network analysis, and sentiment analysis of health content. Section 3 describes the dataset and the proposed AGF-based multimodal framework. Section 4 presents the experimental results and discussion. Finally, Section 5 concludes the paper and outlines directions for future work. 2. title: Examining Dengue-related Information Diffusion on Indonesian Twitter Through Sentiment-based Network Analysis, Spatial Mapping, and Temporal Dynamics
abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited.This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025.Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions.Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98.Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values.Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles.These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis.

License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ Examining Dengue-related Information Diffusion on Indonesian Twitter Through Sentiment-based Network Analysis, Spatial Mapping, and Temporal Dynamics Ribka Devina Margaretha1 Wiwik Anggraeni1* 1Department of Information Systems, Institut Teknologi Sepuluh Nopember, Surabaya, Indonesia * Corresponding author’s Email: wiwik@is.its.ac.id Abstract: Dengue fever remains a major public health challenge in Indonesia, yet studies integrating sentiment analysis, Social Network Analysis, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on social media remain limited. This study proposes an integrated framework applied to 5,715 dengue-related tweets collected from Indonesian Twitter between January 2021 and December 2025. Sentiment classification using IndoBERT revealed a predominantly neutral discourse (65.23%), with meaningful negative (20.31%) and positive (14.45%) proportions. Sentiment-weighted interaction networks were constructed and analysed, revealing highly fragmented structures with modularity scores exceeding 0.98. Healthcare professionals emerged as the most robustly influential actors by betweenness centrality, with PageRank-based influence conditional on self-loop treatment, while the Ministry of Health held the highest in-degree values. Spatial analysis, based primarily on self-reported user locations, indicated geographic concentration along the Java-Bali corridor, and temporal analysis revealed recurring peaks in January and June aligned with Indonesia's wet season and dengue outbreak cycles. These findings demonstrate the value of integrating sentiment, network, and spatial dimensions for comprehensive public health communication analysis. Keywords: Dengue fever, Sentiment-based network analysis, Spatial analysis, Temporal analysis, Social media. 1. Introduction Dengue fever remains one of the fastest- spreading vector-borne diseases and a major global public health challenge, endemic in more than 100 countries and threatening approximately 3.9 billion people, particularly in Southeast Asia and Latin America [1-3]. In Indonesia, dengue is highly endemic and continues to cause serious health problems, with more than 257,000 reported cases and over 1,400 deaths in 2024 [4]. The increasing spread of dengue, driven by climate change, urbanisation, and population growth, has also heightened public concern regarding outbreaks and prevention efforts [5]. The growing use of social media, particularly Twitter, has created new opportunities to observe public responses and information exchange related to disease outbreaks[6-8]. Through mentions, replies, and reposts, Twitter enables rapid information diffusion across communities, while certain accounts play disproportionately influential roles in shaping discussions [9]. Social Network Analysis (SNA) has therefore been widely applied to identify influential actors and examine information diffusion dynamics within online networks [10, 11]. Beyond interaction patterns, social media discussions also reflect public opinions and emotional responses toward ongoing health issues [12]. Sentiment analysis provides a complementary approach for capturing these perceptions, and incorporating sentiment information into network analysis can deepen understanding of how dengue- related discussions propagate and evolve on social media [13]. Dengue burden and public health responses are not uniformly distributed across Indonesia, with substantial disparities observed across provinces and Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 686 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ regions due to differences in population density, climate conditions, healthcare accessibility, and vector control capacity [14, 15]. Public perceptions and responses to health information also vary across communities due to cultural and social differences [16]. These regional variations highlight the importance of incorporating spatial information to better understand geographic differences in dengue- related discussions, public sentiment, and information dissemination patterns. Previous studies have applied SNA to identify influential users and examine information diffusion in online discussions, while sentiment analysis has been widely used to understand public perceptions toward health-related issues, and spatial analysis has been employed to reveal geographic variations in dengue transmission and public health responses. However, these approaches are typically investigated in isolation, limiting a comprehensive understanding of how interaction structures, public sentiment, and geographic context collectively shape online discussions. Studies integrating sentiment-weighted social networks with spatial analysis to examine dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter remain particularly limited, highlighting the need for a more integrated analytical framework. To address this gap, this study integrates sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis to examine dengue-related Twitter discussions, constructing sentiment-weighted interaction networks and analysing them alongside geographic and temporal dimensions. The specific contributions of this study are: • Analysis of the spatial distribution of discussions and sentiments across Indonesian cities • Construction of sentiment-based interaction networks capturing both communication structure and public perception • Identification of national-level influential users using PageRank, degree centrality, and betweenness centrality • Identification of regional influential users across multiple Indonesian cities • Analysis of temporal discussion patterns and sentiment dynamics • Visualisation of interaction networks illustrating information diffusion structures. The remainder of this paper is structured as follows. Section 2 reviews related literature. Section 3 describes the data and methodology. Section 4 presents the results and discussion. Section 5 summarises the findings and outlines future directions. 2. Related works 2.1 Social network analysis for information diffusion SNA has been widely applied to investigate information diffusion and interaction patterns in online social networks, modelling users as nodes and interactions as edges to identify influential actors and community structures [17]. Various approaches have been proposed for influencer detection, including the NetDegree centrality measure and the Weighted Correlated Influence (WCI) model combining user activity and network topology [18, 19]. SNA has also been applied to explore community structures and communication dynamics in domain-specific discussions [20]. In health-related contexts, SNA has been used to identify key influencers, dominant topics, and communication structures shaping public awareness [10, 11, 21]. However, most existing health-related SNA studies focus on network topology and influencer identification without incorporating sentiment context or geographic variation. Bonifazi et al. identified influential users in COVID-19 vaccine Twitter discourse through a multilayer network approach, but did not construct sentiment-segmented networks or examine geographic distributions [21]. Durmaz and Hengirmen applied SNA to vaccine- related Twitter discourse in Turkey using in-degree and betweenness centrality, but did not integrate sentiment labels or examine spatial distributions [22]. Pratiwi et al. combined SNA and sentiment analysis for asthma-related Twitter discourse, but did not link findings to geographic distributions or construct sentiment-segmented networks [10]. The absence of sentiment integration and spatial context in these studies limits the depth of understanding achievable in health-related discourse analysis. 2.2 Sentiment analysis in social media discussions Sentiment analysis is widely applied to understand public opinions in social media, with recent studies demonstrating the effectiveness of advanced language models including IndoBERT for Indonesian-language content [23, 24]. Ishfaq et al. and Eliacik and Erdogan have incorporated sentiment into network-based analyses for influential user identification [25, 26]. However, applications combining sentiment and network characteristics in health-related discussions remain limited. Dengue-specific sentiment studies such as Abdul Ghani et al. demonstrate the value of sentiment for disease surveillance but do not Received: June 15, 2026. Revised: July 16, 2026. 687 International Journal of Intelligent Engineering and Systems, Vol.19, No.9, 2026 DOI: 10.22266/ijies2026.0930.35 This article is licensed under a Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International License. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ construct interaction networks or link findings to geographic distributions [27]. Indonesian-language classification studies such as Supriyadi and Makatita and Nabiilah et al. demonstrate strong model performance without connecting findings to network structures or spatial patterns [23, 24]. While Ishfaq et al. and Eliacik and Erdogan incorporate sentiment into network analyses, neither examined dengue- related discourse or linked findings to spatial distributions [25, 26]. No prior study has simultaneously applied sentiment-integrated SNA to dengue-related Indonesian Twitter data, leaving a gap in understanding how emotional responses and interaction structures collectively shape dengue information diffusion. 2.3 Spatial analysis in health-related studies Spatial analysis has gained increasing attention in public health and social media research for understanding geographic variations in behaviour and information dissemination. Lovera and Cardinale demonstrated that geolocation enriches the interpretation of social media discussions [34]. Similarly, Wu et al. highlighted the value of geospatial enrichment for understanding large-scale sentiment behaviour[35]. In health-related contexts, Lin et al. revealed linguistic and geographic disparities in COVID-19 public awareness through social media, while Zhang et al. applied geographical and temporal analysis to health-related tweets to identify spatiotemporal disease discussion patterns at regional level [36, 37]. However, these studies focus on geographic distribution patterns without modelling user interaction networks or identifying regional-level influential users. Lin et al., Zhang et al., Lovera and Cardinale, and Wu et al. all incorporate geolocation into social media analysis, but do not construct interaction networks, identify influential users, or examine how sentiment varies across network communities [z-37]. Studies applying spatial analysis to dengue-related social media discourse, such as Abdul Ghani et al., have similarly focused on geographic mapping without modelling user interaction dynamics or examining sentiment- segmented network structures [27]. The absence of interaction network modelling and sentiment integration limits understanding of how network dynamics and public sentiment collectively shape dengue information diffusion. 2.4 Research gap Despite the established contributions of SNA, sentiment analysis, and spatial analysis individually, existing health-related social media studies address these dimensions in isolation, as demonstrated across Sections 2.1 to 2.3, focusing on network topology without sentiment context [10, 21, 22], applying sentiment classification without network or spatial linkage[23, 27], or examining geographic patterns without modelling interaction dynamics [34-37]. While sentiment analysis and network approaches have each been applied to health-related social media discourse individually, their simultaneous integration with spatial analysis in the specific context of dengue-related Indonesian Twitter data remains unexplored. No prior study has proposed a unified framework simultaneously capturing the structural, emotional, and geographic dimensions of dengue-related information diffusion on Indonesian Twitter. This study addresses that gap by integrating sentiment analysis, SNA, and spatial analysis within a single framework, constructing sentiment- segmented interaction networks to examine how different emotional contexts shape network structure and influencer profiles, mapping discussion distributions and regional influencer patterns across Indonesian cities, and tracing temporal dynamics of both discussion volume and sentiment evolution over a five-year period. This integrated approach offers a more complete understanding of information dissemination patterns, influential users, and public perceptions across different locations and time periods than prior single-method studies have provided. 3. Materials and method 3.1 Dataset Dengue-related tweets were collected from Twitter (X) between January 2021 and December 2025 using the Scweet Python library with three keywords: "dbd" (dengue haemorrhagic fever acronym in Indonesian), "Aedes aegypti" (the dengue-carrying mosquito species), and "demam berdarah dengue" (dengue haemorrhagic fever). Data collection was conducted between 9-14 April 2026. The collected tweets span the period from January 2021 to December 2025, reflecting the full range of historical tweets retrievable through Scweet at the time of collection; Scweet retrieves historical tweets via browser automation rather than the official Twitter/X API, and collection completeness is therefore subject to the platform's search indexing and any rate-limiting constraints encountered during scraping. All tweets included in this study represent observed data retrieved directly through Scweet; no Received: June 15, 2026. License details: https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by-sa/4.0/ projected, simulated, or placeholder records are included in the dataset or in any reported analysis. Collection was conducted as a series of discrete scraping sessions per keyword and sub-period, with no session returning a tweet count at or exceeding the configured retrieval limit (500-1,000 tweets, depending on keyword), indicating retrieval without truncation within each queried window. A completeness check was performed by examining the year-by-year distribution of collected tweets to confirm the absence of anomalous gaps or artificially uniform collection patterns; as detailed in Section 4.6.1, tweet volume varied organically across the five-year period, consistent with externally documented dengue activity patterns in Indonesia rather than indicating systematic data loss. Each tweet record contains textual content, publication date, user information, engagement statistics, and interaction attributes including mentions, replies, and reposts. The collected dataset serves as the primary source for all sentiment, network, spatial, and temporal analyses conducted in this study. 3.2 Method This study employs an integrated analytical framework consisting of data preprocessing, sentiment classification, network construction, community detection, spatial analysis, and temporal analysis. Data preprocessing The datasets collected from different periods were combined and filtered to retain only the attributes required for analysis, including tweet identifiers, usernames, tweet content, timestamps, language information, location attributes, and interaction metadata. User mentions and replies were extracted separately to support network construction. Duplicate tweets and records with missing values in essential attributes were removed, and tweet texts were cleaned through lowercasing, URL removal, mention and hashtag removal, number and punctuation removal, and whitespace normalisation. Tweets that became empty after cleaning were discarded, and only Indonesian-language tweets were retained. Examples of tweets before and after preprocessing are shown in Table 1. For spatial analysis, location information was obtained from tweet-level and user profile locations, with the latter used as a fallback when tweet-level location was unavailable. Location texts were normalised and matched against a reference dataset of Indonesian cities, with common aliases and abbreviations standardised to improve matching accuracy. This process successfully mapped 3,327 tweets (58.22%) to 168 Indonesian cities. 3.2.2. Sentiment analysis Sentiment analysis was conducted to identify public opinions expressed in dengue-related Twitter discussions. Two pretrained Indonesian sentiment classification models from the Hugging Face library, namely w11wo/indonesian-roberta-base-sentiment- classifier [28] and taufiqdp/indonesian-sentiment (fine-tuned from IndoBERT) [29], were applied to the full cleaned dataset (5,715 tweets) as candidates. full_text: O jornal americano Tampa Bay Times recentemente noticiou a morte de uma idosa em 8 de setembro de 2026. A família dela afirma que os médicos locais atribuíram a morte à dengue, embora o Departamento de Saúde da Flórida ainda não tenha confirmado isso. Essa morte provavelmente fez parte de um surto mais amplo de dengue no condado de Hillsborough, onde houve 95 casos documentados de dengue desde julho de 2026. Em agosto deste ano, o Departamento de Saúde do Condado de Hillsborough emitiu um alerta sobre doenças transmitidas por mosquitos devido a relatos de vários casos adquiridos localmente. Esse aglomerado de casos transmitidos localmente é uma forte lembrança de que uma doença que a maioria dos americanos associa a férias em distantes países tropicais é cada vez mais contraída em casa. A dengue é frequentemente chamada de “febre quebra-ossos”, e esse apelido é merecido. As pessoas que adoecem geralmente apresentam febre alta repentina, acompanhada de forte dor de cabeça, dor atrás dos olhos e dores profundas nos músculos, articulações e ossos. Muitas também sentem náuseas, vomitam ou apresentam erupções cutâneas em manchas alguns dias depois. Como médico especialista em doenças infecciosas e medicina tropical que dirige uma clínica para viajantes, vejo com que facilidade a dengue passa despercebida tanto por pacientes quanto pelos médicos americanos. Em regiões dos EUA onde a doença ainda é pouco comum, ela é facilmente confundida com uma gripe ou a COVID-19, e esse atraso no diagnóstico pode ser perigoso. Esses mosquitos se desenvolvem em cidades com climas quentes e podem se reproduzir em quantidades mínimas de água parada, como em uma tampa de garrafa. E esses mosquitos picam durante o dia, não apenas ao anoitecer. Para os 25% que apresentam sintomas, eles só aparecem de quatro a dez dias após a picada. Uma segunda infecção por um tipo diferente, na verdade, aumenta as chances de desenvolver uma forma grave da doença. Reviravolta com risco de vida A maioria das pessoas sofre com a dengue por uma semana difícil e depois se recupera por conta própria. Mas cerca de um em cada 20 pacientes evolui para dengue grave, uma complicação com risco de vida que tende a ocorrer justamente quando a febre começa a baixar – geralmente entre o terceiro e o sétimo dia, quando os pacientes e suas famílias podem erroneamente supor que o pior já passou. Alguns grupos correm maior risco, incluindo bebês, mulheres grávidas, adultos com mais de 65 anos e pessoas com condições como diabetes, obesidade ou doença renal. Se não for tratada, a dengue grave pode causar a morte de até 10% dos pacientes. Com atendimento hospitalar imediato, esse número cai para menos de um em cada 100 – e é por isso que o diagnóstico precoce é tão importante. Existe uma vacina contra a dengue, mas ela não é recomendada para o turista americano comum. As vacinas disponíveis são usadas apenas em casos específicos, como crianças que moram em áreas de alta transmissão e já tiveram dengue uma vez. Portanto, a prevenção ainda depende principalmente de evitar picadas de mosquito. Como a dengue é tratada Não há medicamento antiviral que cure a dengue. O tratamento consiste em ajudar o organismo enquanto ele combate o vírus. Para pessoas que se sentem bem o suficiente para ficar em casa, isso significa repouso, ingestão abundante de líquidos e paracetamol, comumente conhecido nos EUA pela marca Tylenol, para febre e dor. Pacientes que possam ter dengue devem evitar aspirina, ibuprofeno e outros anti-inflamatórios não esteroides. Esses medicamentos aumentam o risco de sangramento, o que já é um perigo associado à dengue. Pacientes que apresentarem sintomas mais graves precisam ser internados no hospital, onde os médicos administram fluidos intravenosos cuidadosamente dosados e monitoram de perto. Se a quantidade de fluidos for insuficiente, o paciente pode entrar em choque; se for excessiva, os pulmões podem inchar. Um problema global que piora A dengue está em alta em todo o mundo. A Organização Mundial da Saúde (OMS) contabilizou mais de 14 milhões de casos em 2024, o pior ano já registrado, em cerca de 100 países. Isso representa um aumento de 2.600% em relação aos mais de 505 mil casos registrados em 2000. Temperaturas mais altas, o rápido crescimento urbano e as viagens internacionais estão contribuindo para que os mosquitos – e o vírus – se espalhem por lugares onde nunca haviam sido um problema antes. O Sul da Ásia, o Sudeste Asiático e a América Latina são as regiões mais afetadas, mas o problema está se espalhando para o norte. Por que os EUA devem ter atenção A maioria dos casos de dengue nos EUA ainda é contraída no exterior. Os viajantes voltam para casa doentes. Só em 2023, os Centros de Controle e Prevenção de Doenças (CDC) relataram quase 1.900 casos desse tipo relacionados a viagens. Mas cada viajante infectado é uma faísca, e nos estados de clima quente o combustível já está presente. Nos territórios dos EUA, Porto Rico e as Ilhas Virgens Americanas registram, de longe, o maior número de casos. A Flórida apresenta o maior risco entre os 50 estados, com o condado de Miami-Dade registrando mais de 300 infecções por dengue adquiridas localmente entre 2010 e 2024. Casos locais também surgiram no Texas, na Califórnia, no Arizona e no Havaí. Descanse, beba líquidos e use paracetamol – não ibuprofeno nem aspirina. Acima de tudo, fique atento aos sinais de alerta. Dor abdominal intensa, vômitos repetidos, sangramento ou sonolência repentina significam que você deve ir imediatamente a um pronto-socorro. E para proteger a si mesmo e aos seus vizinhos: use repelente de insetos, vista roupas de mangas compridas e esvazie qualquer água parada no seu quintal onde os mosquitos possam se reproduzir.

full_text: The Tampa Bay Times reported the death of an elderly woman on Sept. 8, 2026. Her family says local doctors attributed her death to dengue fever, although the Florida Department of Health has not yet confirmed that. This death was likely part of a larger dengue outbreak in Hillsborough County, where there have been 95 documented cases of dengue since July 2026. In August, the Hillsborough County Health Department issued a mosquito-borne illness alert due to reports of multiple locally acquired cases. This cluster of locally spread cases is a stark reminder that a disease which most Americans associate with faraway tropical vacations is increasingly being caught at home. Dengue is often called “breakbone fever,” and the nickname is earned. People who get sick typically develop a sudden high fever along with a pounding headache, pain behind the eyes and deep aches in the muscles, joints and bones. Many also feel nauseated, throw up or break out in a blotchy rash a few days in. As an infectious diseases physician and tropical medicine specialist who directs a travel clinic, I see how easily dengue slips past both patients and doctors. In parts of the U.S. where the disease is still uncommon, it is easily mistaken for the flu or COVID-19, and that delay can be dangerous. How it spreads Dengue is not passed from person to person like a cold. It spreads through the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes, mainly Aedes aegypti, a species commonly found in Florida. These mosquitoes thrive in warm cities and can breed in as little as a bottle capful of standing water. These mosquitoes bite during the day, not just at dusk. The cycle is simple and hard to break: A mosquito bites an infected person, then bites someone else days later, giving them the virus. Dengue is especially tricky because most infections cause no symptoms at all. Roughly 3 in 4 people who catch the virus never feel sick. For the 25% who are symptomatic, those symptoms don’t appear until four to 10 days after being bitten. In addition, there are four different strains of the dengue virus, and surviving one gives you lasting protection against only that one. A second infection with a different type actually raises the odds of severe disease. A life-threatening turn Most people suffer with dengue for a miserable week and then recover on their own. But about 1 in 20 patients progress to severe dengue, a life-threatening turn that tends to strike just as the fever breaks – often around days three to seven, when patients and their families may wrongly assume the worst is over. In severe dengue, tiny blood vessels throughout the body start leaking fluid, blood pressure can crash and dangerous bleeding or organ damage can follow. Warning signs that someone is sliding into this phase include severe belly pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding from the gums or nose, extreme drowsiness or restlessness, and blood in vomit or stool. Some groups face higher risk, including infants, pregnant women, adults over 65 and people with conditions like diabetes, obesity or kidney disease. Left untreated, severe dengue can kill up to 10% of patients. With prompt hospital care, that number drops below 1 in 100 – which is why recognizing it early matters so much. A dengue vaccine exists, but it is not recommended for the average American traveler. The available shots are used only in select cases, such as children who live in high-transmission areas and have already had dengue once. So prevention still rests mostly on avoiding mosquito bites. How dengue is treated There is no antiviral drug that cures dengue. Care is all about supporting the body while it fights the virus. For people well enough to stay home, that means rest, plenty of fluids and acetaminophen, commonly known in the U.S. by the brand name Tylenol, for fever and pain. Patients who may have dengue must avoid aspirin, ibuprofen and other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. These drugs raise the risk of bleeding, which is already a danger with dengue. Patients who develop more severe symptoms need to be admitted to the hospital, where doctors give carefully measured intravenous fluids and watch closely. Too little fluid and the patient can go into shock; too much and the lungs can flood. A worsening global problem Dengue is surging worldwide. The World Health Organization recorded more than 14 million cases in 2024, its worst year on record, across some 100 countries. That’s a 2,600% increase from the more than 505,000 cases reported in 2000. Warmer temperatures, rapid urban growth and global travel are all helping the mosquitoes – and the virus – expand into places where it has never been a problem before. South Asia, Southeast Asia and Latin America carry the heaviest burden, but the map is spreading north. Why the U.S. should pay attention Most U.S. dengue cases are still picked up abroad. Travelers return home sick. In 2023 alone, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported nearly 1,900 such travel-related cases. But every infected traveler is a spark, and in warm states the tinder is already there. In the U.S. territories, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands see the most cases by far. Florida has the highest risk among the 50 states, with Miami-Dade County recording more than 300 locally acquired dengue infections between 2010 and 2024. Local cases have also turned up in Texas, California, Arizona and Hawaii. What to do if you think you have dengue If you develop a sudden fever after traveling to a dengue-prone area, or after mosquito exposure in South Florida, see a doctor and mention where you’ve been. Rest, drink fluids and use acetaminophen – not ibuprofen or aspirin. Most importantly, watch for the warning signs. Severe belly pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding or sudden drowsiness means get to an emergency room right away. And to protect yourself and your neighbors: Use insect repellent, wear long sleeves and dump out any standing water in your yard where mosquitoes breed.

Smith Collection/Gado/Getty Images Dengue‐carrying mosquitoes expand their reach into new territories – including Florida Published: September 15, 2026 8:35am EDT The Tampa Bay Times reported the death of an elderly woman on Sept. 8, 2026. Her family says local doctors attributed her death to dengue fever, although the Florida Department of Health has not yet confirmed that. This death was likely part of a larger dengue outbreak in Hillsborough County, where there have been 95 documented cases of dengue since July 2026. In August, the Hillsborough County Health Department issued a mosquito-borne illness alert due to reports of multiple locally acquired cases. This cluster of locally spread cases is a stark reminder that a disease which most Americans associate with faraway tropical vacations is increasingly being caught at home. Dengue is often called “breakbone fever,” and the nickname is earned. People who get sick typically develop a sudden high fever along with a pounding headache, pain behind the eyes and deep aches in the muscles, joints and bones. Many also feel nauseated, throw up or break out in a blotchy rash a few days in. As an infectious diseases physician and tropical medicine specialist who directs a travel clinic, I see how easily dengue slips past both patients and doctors. In parts of the U.S. where the disease is still uncommon, it is easily mistaken for the flu or COVID-19, and that delay can be dangerous. How it spreads Dengue is not passed from person to person like a cold. It spreads through the bite of infected Aedes mosquitoes, mainly Aedes aegypti, a species commonly found in Florida. These mosquitoes thrive in warm cities and can breed in as little as a bottle capful of standing water. These mosquitoes bite during the day, not just at dusk. The cycle is simple and hard to break: A mosquito bites an infected person, then bites someone else days later, giving them the virus. Dengue is especially tricky because most infections cause no symptoms at all. Roughly 3 in 4 people who catch the virus never feel sick. For the 25% who are symptomatic, those symptoms don’t appear until four to 10 days after being bitten. In addition, there are four different strains of the dengue virus, and surviving one gives you lasting protection against only that one. A second infection with a different type actually raises the odds of severe disease. A life-threatening turn Most people suffer with dengue for a miserable week and then recover on their own. But about 1 in 20 patients progress to severe dengue, a life-threatening turn that tends to strike just as the fever breaks – often around days three to seven, when patients and their families may wrongly assume the worst is over. In severe dengue, tiny blood vessels throughout the body start leaking fluid, blood pressure can crash and dangerous bleeding or organ damage can follow. Warning signs that someone is sliding into this phase include severe belly pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding from the gums or nose, extreme drowsiness or restlessness, and blood in vomit or stool. Some groups face higher risk, including infants, pregnant women, adults over 65 and people with conditions like diabetes, obesity or kidney disease. Left untreated, severe dengue can kill up to 10% of patients. With prompt hospital care, that number drops below 1 in 100 – which is why recognizing it early matters so much. A dengue vaccine exists, but it is not recommended for the average American traveler. The available shots are used only in select cases, such as children who live in high-transmission areas and have already had dengue once. So prevention still rests mostly on avoiding mosquito bites. How dengue is treated There is no antiviral drug that cures dengue. Care is all about supporting the body while it fights the virus. For people well enough to stay home, that means rest, plenty of fluids and acetaminophen, commonly known in the U.S. by the brand name Tylenol, for fever and pain. Patients who may have dengue must avoid aspirin, ibuprofen and other non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs. These drugs raise the risk of bleeding, which is already a danger with dengue. Patients who develop more severe symptoms need to be admitted to the hospital, where doctors give carefully measured intravenous fluids and watch closely. Too little fluid and the patient can go into shock; too much and the lungs can flood. A worsening global problem Dengue is surging worldwide. The World Health Organization recorded more than 14 million cases in 2024, its worst year on record, across some 100 countries. That’s a 2,600% increase from the more than 505,000 cases reported in 2000. Warmer temperatures, rapid urban growth and global travel are all helping the mosquitoes – and the virus – expand into places where it has never been a problem before. South Asia, Southeast Asia and Latin America carry the heaviest burden, but the map is spreading north. Why the U.S. should pay attention Most U.S. dengue cases are still picked up abroad. Travelers return home sick. In 2023 alone, the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention reported nearly 1,900 such travel-related cases. But every infected traveler is a spark, and in warm states the tinder is already there. In the U.S. territories, Puerto Rico and the U.S. Virgin Islands see the most cases by far. Florida has the highest risk among the 50 states, with Miami-Dade County recording more than 300 locally acquired dengue infections between 2010 and 2024. Local cases have also turned up in Texas, California, Arizona and Hawaii. What to do if you think you have dengue If you develop a sudden fever after traveling to a dengue-prone area, or after mosquito exposure in South Florida, see a doctor and mention where you’ve been. Rest, drink fluids and use acetaminophen – not ibuprofen or aspirin. Most importantly, watch for the warning signs. Severe belly pain, repeated vomiting, bleeding or sudden drowsiness means get to an emergency room right away. And to protect yourself and your neighbors: Use insect repellent, wear long sleeves and dump out any standing water in your yard where mosquitoes breed.
